stories.headline: Moonshot releases 2.8‑trillion‑parameter Kimi K3 model weights
stories.summary: Moonshot AI has published the 1.56 TB weight files for its Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion‑parameter language model. The release continues the project’s unconventional MIT‑style license first introduced with K2.

stories.headline: Show HN: XY – GPU‑accelerated, composable charts built in Rust
stories.summary: XY is an open‑source Rust library that renders charts on the GPU for speed and composability. The project has drawn modest Hacker News interest as a high‑performance alternative to existing charting tools.

stories.headline: Kimi K3 Architecture Overview and Technical Notes
stories.summary: Sebastian Raschka details the internal design of the Kimi K3 model, covering its transformer stack, training pipeline, and performance trade‑offs. The notes serve as a practical guide for researchers probing trillion‑parameter architectures.

stories.headline: Formally verified 3D CSG implementation in Lean 4
stories.summary: A new Lean 4 library provides a formally verified constructive solid geometry operation, guaranteeing mesh intersection correctness against a concise specification. It showcases how formal methods can replace large, error‑prone AI‑generated geometry code.

stories.headline: Fast remediation becomes the new security trust model (JFrog‑OpenAI collaboration)
stories.summary: JFrog teamed with OpenAI to automatically surface zero‑day vulnerabilities and speed up patch deployment. The article argues that AI‑driven rapid remediation should replace legacy trust models in modern cybersecurity.

stories.headline: Jen Wilkin’s new book urges believers to view aging as spiritual deepening
stories.summary: Wilkin reframes aging from a narrative of decline to one of biblical deepening, offering scriptural insight and practical steps. Her guide aims to help Christians embrace later life with purpose and joy.

stories.headline: A muted culture calls for fresh evangelism strategies
stories.summary: The author claims today’s culture muffles the perception of creation, demanding innovative outreach methods. Emphasizing general revelation, the piece urges churches to rekindle attentiveness to the natural world.

stories.headline: Netanyahu to meet Trump in first encounter since Iran war began
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to meet former President Donald Trump amid mounting domestic pressures for both leaders. The summit arrives as Netanyahu seeks reelection and Trump grapples with criticism over the ongoing war.

stories.headline: Japan earthquake: key facts from the Kyushu quake
stories.summary: A strong tremor struck Kyushu island, causing extensive damage and prompting nationwide alerts. Officials are tallying casualties, assessing infrastructure loss, and monitoring for aftershocks.

stories.headline: Why Netanyahu’s White House visit with Trump carries high stakes
stories.summary: The upcoming meeting is fraught with diplomatic tension as U.S. public support for Israel declines. Both leaders must balance domestic criticism while addressing broader regional security concerns.

stories.headline: Jobs Declares Apple’s Products Are Built for Users, Not Advertisers
stories.summary: At WWDC 2011, Steve Jobs highlighted Apple’s ad‑free philosophy, contrasting iCloud email with free services that embed ads. He emphasized that Apple creates tools it would use itself, rejecting ad‑driven models.

stories.headline: Simon Willison Maps the Evolving Landscape of AI Model Choices
stories.summary: Willison’s post surveys the latest generative AI options, from ChatGPT and Claude to Gemini, noting how recommendations shift as new versions appear. He also points readers to alternative research‑oriented tools like Deep Research.

stories.headline: Practical Guide to Profiling eBPF Programs
stories.summary: Naveen Srivasan walks through techniques for measuring performance of eBPF code, covering tooling, metrics, and common pitfalls. The article helps developers pinpoint bottlenecks in kernel‑level scripts.

stories.headline: Tokens Become the Energy Meter of the AI Economy
stories.summary: Economists are treating AI usage tokens like kilowatt‑hours, using them to gauge how much AI power is consumed across sectors. The metric offers a standardized way to track AI’s economic footprint.

stories.headline: Inside Zig’s Incremental Compilation Engine
stories.summary: Martin Lugg dissects how Zig tracks source changes to recompile only what’s necessary, boosting build speed. The post details dependency graphs, hashing, and cache strategies that power the feature.

stories.headline: Flashpaper: One‑Time Secret Sharing Without a Database
stories.summary: Min from Bangkok introduces a tool that creates encrypted messages that self‑destruct after being read, eliminating persistent storage. The project mimics a dead‑man’s switch and aims for spy‑movie‑style data disappearance.

stories.headline: GrapheneOS Stands by Data‑Wipe Feature That Thwarts Border Searches
stories.summary: After U.S. Customs attempted to access a phone, GrapheneOS defended its remote‑wipe capability that erases data on demand. The controversy highlights tensions between privacy‑focused OSes and law‑enforcement demands.

stories.headline: UTM Reports Bridged Network Failure on Apple M5 Pro Macs
stories.summary: Users of the UTM virtualization app find that VMs refuse to start when the network is set to Bridged mode on M5 Pro hardware. The issue appears tied to Apple’s new silicon networking stack and is tracked on GitHub.

stories.headline: Critique: Satire on ‘Yesteryear’ Misses the Mark on Christian Womanhood
stories.summary: The review argues that the piece’s attempt at satire fails because it lacks a nuanced understanding of the traditions it mocks. It calls for deeper engagement rather than shallow ridicule.

stories.headline: Pitchfork Reviews ‘Reality Awaits’: Auto‑Tuned Doom Meets Sharp Lyricism
stories.summary: The seventh album from the rock band blends heavy auto‑tuned vocals with incisive, dark lyrics, delivering a strange yet cohesive statement. Critics note the record leans into its theatricality while maintaining musical depth.

stories.headline: Beard’s Third Solo Album Marries Lush Arrangements with Self‑Discovery
stories.summary: The record serves as a celebration of the artist’s growing self‑knowledge, pairing rich instrumentation with a relaxed vibe. It feels like a comfortable, reflective journey through his experiences.

stories.headline: Jilian Medford’s Fifth Album Confronts Stagnation and Heartbreak
stories.summary: On “Shiverstruck,” Medford weaves subdued indie pop with vivid allusions to emotional turbulence and a cross‑country move. The songs balance melancholy lyrics with breezy melodies, capturing the tension between inertia and change.

stories.headline: Patagonian Soundscapes Shape Argentinian Producer’s ‘Tesoros’
stories.summary: The album stitches field recordings from daily walks around Patagonian lakes into delicate electronic sketches. The result is a nostalgic tribute that blends organic ambience with a hint of twee synth charm.

stories.headline: Guide to Building Your Own Game Engine (2023)
stories.summary: The post walks readers through the core components and design decisions needed to craft a custom game engine, emphasizing modular architecture and performance trade‑offs. Community comments discuss practical pitfalls and resources for indie developers.

stories.headline: Scientists Edge Toward a Unified Theory of Musical Harmony
stories.summary: The 2012 arXiv paper proposes a formal framework that quantifies harmonic relationships using mathematical models. It sparked extensive discussion on Hacker News about its implications for music theory and AI composition.

stories.headline: EU Initiative Calls for Ban on Digital IDs and Age Verification
stories.summary: The Citizens’ Initiative urges European lawmakers to reject mandatory digital identification and age‑check systems, warning they threaten internet freedom. The proposal argues such measures could erode privacy and open the web to censorship.

stories.headline: Experimental HIV Vaccine Shows Record‑Breaking Efficacy in Animals
stories.summary: Researchers report a vaccine candidate that achieved unprecedented protection levels in preclinical trials, sparking optimism for human studies. The breakthrough leverages a novel immunogen design that elicits broad neutralizing antibodies.

stories.headline: Second Shooting at U.S. Consulate in Toronto Prompts High‑Speed Chase
stories.summary: Police pursued a suspect after gunfire struck the consulate, but the individual evaded capture and remains at large. Earlier this year, three people were arrested following a similar attack.

stories.headline: Madrid Region Battles Triple Wildfire Threat Amid Incoming Heatwave
stories.summary: Three separate fires are raging in the Madrid area, prompting emergency measures as a scorching heatwave approaches. Authorities warn conditions could worsen, heightening concerns for residents and ecosystems.

stories.headline: China’s Flood and Storm Crises Amplified by AI‑Generated Fake Footage
stories.summary: Recent natural disasters in China have been accompanied by a surge of synthetic videos circulating online, confusing the public. Experts note the challenge of distinguishing authentic coverage from AI‑fabricated content.

stories.headline: Zelensky and Netanyahu to Meet White House Amid Graham Funeral
stories.summary: The Ukrainian and Israeli leaders will travel to Washington for separate Oval Office talks on regional conflicts, timing coinciding with Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral that has drawn both delegations to the capital.

stories.headline: Xenharmlib Music Theory Library Adds Just Intonation Support
stories.summary: The open‑source Xenharmlib now includes tools for just intonation, allowing composers to work with pure intervals. The update expands the library’s capabilities for microtonal and historically informed music creation.

stories.headline: New Kimi Delta Attention Model Proposed for Efficient AI
stories.summary: Researchers introduce Kimi Delta Attention, a technique that reduces computational load while preserving performance in transformer models. The approach promises faster training and inference for large language models.

stories.headline: ‘Ricochet’ Shows How Gun Rights Are Expanding as Laws Tighten
stories.summary: A New York Times investigation reveals the firearms industry and the NRA are redefining the Second Amendment, targeting youth culture and a new brand of masculinity. Meanwhile, legislative efforts to restrict guns are facing setbacks.

stories.headline: U.S. Walks Out of UN Security Council as France Speaks
stories.summary: The United States abruptly left a Security Council session while France delivered remarks, after the U.S., North Korea and Russia voted against extending the UN human‑rights commissioner’s term. The incident highlighted growing diplomatic tensions.

stories.headline: Trump to Meet Zelenskyy and Netanyahu; TPS Holders Face Deportation Threat
stories.summary: Former President Trump scheduled separate meetings with Ukraine’s Zelenskyy and Israel’s Netanyahu to discuss policy, while the administration signaled that Temporary Protected Status recipients could soon be slated for removal. The moves come amid heightened immigration debates.

stories.headline: Democrats Push Anti‑Corruption Reforms After Trump Ethics Breaches
stories.summary: In response to perceived ethical violations by Trump, Democrats are urging comprehensive anti‑corruption legislation to restore public trust. They argue that systemic reforms are needed to curb influence‑peddling and protect voters.

stories.headline: Setup Script Updated to Handle Git Worktrees
stories.summary: A new blog post outlines enhancements to a setup script, enabling it to work with Git worktrees for more flexible repository management. The guide provides step‑by‑step instructions for developers adopting this workflow.

stories.headline: J&J Proposes $5.5 B Settlement Over Baby Powder Cancer Claims
stories.summary: Johnson & Johnson has offered up to $5.5 billion to resolve lawsuits alleging its talc‑based baby powder caused cancer. The deal aims to end a protracted legal battle spanning decades.

stories.headline: Seattle Food Festival Shooting Suspects Count Rises to Three
stories.summary: Authorities report three individuals linked to the fatal shooting at a Seattle food festival; one is in custody, another is being sought, and a third is believed to have died at the scene. The investigation continues as officials release new court documents.

stories.headline: Japanese town wrestles with identity after first mosque sparks protests
stories.summary: The coastal community is confronting how to blend a growing foreign workforce with its traditional culture. Local residents clash over the new mosque, highlighting broader questions of religious integration in Japan.

stories.headline: Ecuadorian gang leader faces BBC's Orla Guerin on drug war and police infiltration
stories.summary: Guerin sits down with a notorious gang boss to discuss the surge in violence and cocaine trafficking. The interview reveals how criminal groups have penetrated law‑enforcement ranks, complicating the nation's drug battle.

stories.headline: 'A La Carte' July 28 roundup: faith, media, tech detox and workplace truth‑telling
stories.summary: The latest issue mixes pieces on protecting sheep from overbearing pastors, scrutiny of Ligonier Ministries and CNN, and the pressure on employees to lie for bosses. It also offers a teen tech‑detox guide, reflections on faithful femininity, and light‑hearted self‑parody.

stories.headline: Roberto Mancini back as Italy coach after Pirlo steps aside and Maldini quits
stories.summary: Mancini has been reappointed to lead the Azzurri just a day after former star Andrea Pirlo ruled himself out of the job. The reshuffle also sees technical director Paolo Maldini resign, leaving the federation in flux.

stories.headline: Zinedine Zidane named head coach of France national team
stories.summary: The former Real Madrid and France captain has been confirmed as the new manager of Les Bleus. Zidane inherits a squad seeking to rebuild after recent disappointments on the international stage.

stories.headline: UEFA lashes out at FIFA's plan to bring private investors into World Cup
stories.summary: European football's governing body condemned Gianni Infantino's proposal to seek private capital for its flagship tournaments. UEFA warned the move could undermine the sport's integrity and its own authority.

stories.headline: BBC follows Ecuador's police as they battle cocaine superhighway to Europe
stories.summary: Reporters ride along with officers confronting a massive surge in cocaine shipments bound for European markets. The investigation highlights the power of local gangs and the challenges faced by law‑enforcement in curbing the flow.

stories.headline: Magnitude‑7.1 quake rattles Kyushu, collapses shopping mall and traps shoppers
stories.summary: A strong tremor struck Japan's southern island, causing a shopping centre to cave in and leaving dozens trapped. Emergency crews rushed to the scene, treating the injured and searching for survivors.

stories.headline: Seattle honors three victims of food‑festival shooting as 'lovers of life'
stories.summary: The city gathered to remember the three people killed in a tragic shooting at a local food festival. Speakers highlighted the victims' vibrant spirits and the community's resolve to heal.

stories.headline: French warship fires 17 rounds during live BBC interview with Chris Philp
stories.summary: While being interviewed, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp watched a naval vessel conduct a shooting drill, discharging 17 shells. The unexpected demonstration underscored the tension between political discourse and military readiness.
